root_cause: High-frequency pg_cron jobs were aligned on the same minute boundaries while cron.use_background_workers=off, so each concurrent run consumed a database connection. Under load this caused pg_cron job startup timeouts, Supavisor session-pool checkout timeouts, and PostgREST schema-cache statement timeouts. Noncritical bg-interactie telemetry then amplified the incident by continuing to send a high volume of REST inserts during Data API degradation.
contributing_causes: The project has max_connections=60 while pg_cron allows up to 32 concurrent jobs.
Five */5 jobs, three */10 jobs, two */15 jobs, six hourly jobs at minute 17, and five daily jobs around 06:20 created deterministic fan-out peaks.
GitHub-hosted runners cannot rely on the project's direct IPv6 database endpoint; trusted migration repair must use the IPv4 Supavisor session pooler.
prevention_rule: Spread database-backed cron schedules so recurring control-plane load stays bounded; keep GitHub database transport on the canonical IPv4 Supavisor session bridge; and make noncritical telemetry fail-open with a short Data API timeout and circuit breaker.

incident: Supavisor ECHECKOUTTIMEOUT after 15000ms in Session mode
Supavisor DB connection timeout to the project's IPv6 address on port 5432
PostgREST failed schema-cache reload with PostgreSQL 57014 statement timeout
pg_cron job startup timeouts across the 1m/5m/10m/15m clusters
hundreds of bg-interactie(s) edge/Data-API events per minute during the incident
recovery: 26 cron schedules were staggered without removing their intended cadence
the 1-minute watchdog/reconciliation jobs returned to sub-second successful runs
PostgREST reconnected and loaded its schema cache successfully
bg-interactie v6 uses a 2500ms Data API budget and a 30s in-memory circuit breaker
supabase-migration-repair-bridge v4 canonicalizes direct DB input to aws-0-eu-central-1.pooler.supabase.com:5432 and reports supavisor-session-ipv4
